objective-qualitative.why: Both objectives are qualitative, aspirational statements about user experience ('daily habit users genuinely look forward to opening', 'trusted, opt-in channel') with Q3 2025 time-bounding. Neither is a metric or a task.

krs-are-outcomes.why: All KRs are behavioural metrics: sessions/user/week, DAU, D7 retention, feed engagement rate, opt-in rate, notification-driven session rate, opt-out rate. No feature shipping tasks are listed as KRs; the note explicitly calls out that shipping is excluded.

baseline-to-target.why: Most KRs have explicit baselines and targets. However, KR3 in Obj 1 and KR2/KR3 in Obj 2 list baselines as 'Establish baseline in wk 1' — these are unanchored at submission time. The document acknowledges this and provides a mitigation plan, but the criterion requires each KR to have a baseline, which three do not yet satisfy.

laddering.why: A clear 'Ladders up to' section explicitly connects both objectives to the company goal of growing engagement across the product.

guardrail.why: Each objective has explicit guardrails: crash rate ≤0.5% and uninstall rate not increasing for Obj 1; push send volume ≤5/user/week and app store rating floor for Obj 2. These prevent gaming the KRs by degrading other dimensions.

not-vanity-not-sandbagged.why: Raw totals are explicitly avoided (no total sessions, no MAU, no total pushes). DAU is the one absolute number but paired with per-user rates. Targets (~35% session lift, 23% DAU lift, 10pp opt-in) are stretch but contextually justified. The document proactively flags the rationale for each target.

focused.why: Two objectives, four KRs in Obj 1 and three in Obj 2 — within the 1-3 objectives / 3-5 KRs guideline. The set is coherent and thematically tight.
